intro: Nouns whose meaning changes with their gender, nouns that never change, and awkward plurals.
p.la víctima.nota: Always feminine, also for a man.
p.el personaje.nota: Always masculine, also for a woman.
b1.texto:
**Same word, two genders, two meanings.** The article is the only clue: **el orden** (tidiness) and **la orden** (a command); **el capital** (money) and **la capital** (city); **el cura** (priest) and **la cura** (cure); **el frente** (front) and **la frente** (forehead); **el cometa** (comet) and **la cometa** (kite); **el coma** and **la coma**; **el editorial** (article) and **la editorial** (publisher); **el guía** (a guide who is a man) and **la guía** (a guidebook, or a guide who is a woman).

**Trees and fruit.** The tree is masculine, the fruit feminine: **el manzano** / **la manzana**; **el naranjo** / **la naranja**; **el cerezo** / **la cereza**; **el olivo** / **la oliva**.

**One form for both sexes.** The article changes: **el / la testigo**, **el / la periodista**, **el / la cantante**, **el / la joven**.

**One gender for both sexes.** The article does not change: **la víctima**, **la persona**, **el personaje**, **el bebé**. You say **Juan fue la víctima**.

**Feminine endings.** Nouns in **-ción**, **-sión**, **-dad**, **-tad**, **-tud**, **-ez** and **-umbre** are feminine: **la costumbre**, **la timidez**, **la actitud**.

**Masculine in -ma.** Many words of Greek origin: **el problema**, **el tema**, **el sistema**, **el clima**, **el idioma**, **el programa**, **el síntoma**.

**Plurals.**

- Words in **-s** with the stress before the last syllable do not change: **la crisis** / **las crisis**; **el análisis** / **los análisis**; **el virus** / **los virus**; **el lunes** / **los lunes**.
- Words ending in stressed **-í** or **-ú** take **-es** or **-s**: **esquí** → **esquís** or **esquíes**.
- The stress moves in a few: **el régimen** → **los regímenes**; **el carácter** → **los caracteres**.

**Capital letters** can change the meaning: **la Tierra** (the planet) and **la tierra** (soil); **el Estado** (the State) and **el estado** (condition).
b2.f0: I've received an order from the boss: he wants the warehouse tidy before Monday.
b2.f1: Well, I have another problem. The publisher wants the editorial from me by tomorrow.
b2.f3: On this year's two crises. The main victim, according to the analyses, has been small business.
b2.f4: Be careful with the commas. Last time the proofreader gave you the text back full of corrections.
b2.f5: I know. And that was with only one comma missing. There are characters in this office who forgive nothing.
b5.pregunta: Which sentence is correct about a man called Pedro?
b6.pregunta: Complete: the country has lived through several crises.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Words in unstressed -is do not change in the plural.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Crisis does not change in the plural.
b7.pregunta: Complete: the fruit of the apple tree.
b7.o0.refuerzo: The tree is masculine: el manzano.
b8.pregunta: El cura and la cura are…
b9.o0: He has a scar on his forehead.
b9.o1: He has a scar at the front.
b9.o1.explicacion: La frente is the forehead. El frente is the front.
b9.o2: He has an appointment in front.
b9.o2.explicacion: Cicatriz is a scar, and la frente is the forehead.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The stress moves forward one syllable.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write ten sentences in which the gender of a noun changes its meaning, and a short text using five of them.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud, with examples, five nouns that foreigners often get wrong in gender.
